subject: 110 Brooks Street Significance Determination
overview: The Commission conducted demolition delay reviews for three residential properties and initiated preliminary planning for Medford's 400th anniversary and upcoming cemetery preservation projects.

items.title: 18 Cherry Street Determination of Significance
items.summary: The Commission found the property not significant because, despite its age, extensive alterations and additions have obscured its historical architectural character. Approved a motion to allow the demolition for a proposed multi-unit townhouse development.

items.title: 106 Alexander Avenue Determination of Significance
items.summary: Approved the demolition application as complete and found the 1920s residence not significant.

items.title: 110 Brooks Street Determination of Significance
items.summary: The Commission found the property significant due to its association with architect Aaron Gould and its potential contribution to a future historic district. A public hearing was scheduled for October 7 to address the project, which had already undergone interior demolition following a permitting error by the city's building department.

items.title: Salem Street Burying Ground Flagpole Replacement
items.summary: The Commission requested that the city hire an archaeologist to monitor the excavation for a new flagpole given the unknown locations of burials on the site.

items.title: Medford Historical Society Partnership and 400th Anniversary Planning
items.summary: Members discussed co-sponsoring an archaeology lecture in December and the urgent need to establish a collaborative planning committee and budget for Medford's 400th anniversary in 2030.

items.title: Preservation Training and Workshops
items.summary: Announced several upcoming Massachusetts Historical Commission workshops regarding significance and architectural research.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from the July meeting, August regular meeting, and the August special meeting.

items.title: Subcommittee and Form B Documentation Updates
items.summary: Commissioners updated the status of properties under demolition delay and ordered historical documentation for 55 Myrtle Street.

items.title: Building Department Coordination and Permitting Process
items.summary: Jennifer Keenan reported on efforts to fine-tune the city's automated permitting system to ensure all major renovations are routed for Commission review to prevent future procedural errors.

items.title: Cemetery Preservation Surveys and Grant Applications
items.summary: Received updates on headstone documentation at Cross Street and Oak Grove cemeteries and discussed applying for state Survey and Planning grants for an Oak Grove master plan.

items.title: Thomas Brooks Park Public Meeting
items.summary: Scheduled a digital public meeting for late October to share progress on the phase two grant funding for sidewalks, signage, and archaeological capping.

items.title: Brooks Estate Administrative Position
items.summary: Announced a grant-funded contract for an administrative professional, noting a requirement that applicants must be Medford residents.
